nodes.name: Olympias Deposit
nodes.definition: Gold deposit in Greece mentioned in the context of refractory gold ore processing and referenced in the monograph of Lodeischikov.
nodes.text: Olympias Deposit (Olympias)

nodes.name: Pezinok Deposit
nodes.definition: Gold deposit in Slovakia cited in the technological classification and processing of refractory gold ores.
nodes.text: Pezinok Deposit (Pezinok)

nodes.name: Porgera Gold Plant
nodes.definition: Industrial gold processing plant in Papua New Guinea that uses pressure oxidation (autoclave) for refractory gold ores. Referenced in literature for autoclave oxidation technology and commissioning of the pressure oxidation circuit.
nodes.text: Porgera Gold Plant (Porgera plant (Papua New Guinea), Porgera pressure oxidation circuit)

nodes.name: Sarylah Gold-Antimony Deposit
nodes.definition: Комплексное золото-сурьмяное месторождение, руды которого содержат свободное золото, антимонит, арсенопирит и сурьмяные оксиды. Является сырьевой базой для Сарылахской обогатительной фабрики, на которой разработана комбинированная гравитационно-флотационная схема с получением лигатурного золота и коллективного золото-сурьмяного концентрата.
nodes.text: Sarylah Gold-Antimony Deposit (Сарылахское месторождение, Сарлах, Sarylah deposit)

nodes.name: Snow Lake Deposit
nodes.definition: Gold deposit in Canada referenced in the monograph on gold and silver recovery from refractory ores.
nodes.text: Snow Lake Deposit (Snow Lake)

nodes.name: Sukhoy Log Gold Deposit
nodes.definition: A large gold deposit in Russia (Irkutsk region) known for its carbonaceous shale-hosted refractory gold ore. Pilot tests using heavy medium separation were conducted by Irgiredmet and VNIItsvetmet on a 912 t sample.
nodes.text: Sukhoy Log Gold Deposit (Сухой Лог, Sukhoy Log deposit)

nodes.name: Stepnyak Deposit
nodes.definition: Gold deposit in Kazakhstan mentioned in the context of refractory gold ore processing technology.
nodes.text: Stepnyak Deposit (Stepnyak)

nodes.name: Taseevskaya Gold Processing Plant
nodes.definition: A gold processing plant in Russia (Chita region) whose flotation tailings were treated by sorption-flotation technology to recover residual gold. The process achieved 50.8% gold extraction into a carbonaceous concentrate.
nodes.text: Taseevskaya Gold Processing Plant (Тасеевская ЗИФ, Taseevskaya ZIF)

nodes.name: Tereksai Gold Deposit
nodes.definition: A gold deposit in Russia (possibly Kyrgyzstan) containing antimonite as a chemical depressant and gold-bearing pyrite within a carbonaceous-sulfide host rock, representing a mixed refractory ore type.
nodes.text: Tereksai Gold Deposit (Терексайское месторождение, Tereksai deposit)

nodes.name: Torbrit Deposit
nodes.definition: Gold deposit in Canada referenced in the literature on processing of refractory gold ores.
nodes.text: Torbrit Deposit (Torbrit)

nodes.name: Hakandzhinskoe Deposit
nodes.definition: Gold deposit in Russia (Magadan region) included in the index of the monograph on refractory gold ore processing.
nodes.text: Hakandzhinskoe Deposit (Hakandzhinskoe)

nodes.name: Eskay Creek Project
nodes.definition: A gold-silver project in British Columbia, Canada, for which process development was carried out including pressure oxidation. Mentioned in the context of hydrometallurgical research.
nodes.text: Eskay Creek Project (Eskay Creek mine (Canada), Eskay Creek gold-silver project)

nodes.name: Itogon Gold Plant (Philippines)
nodes.definition: A gold processing plant on Luzon Island, Philippines, with a capacity of 600 t/d, treating pyritic gold ore by flotation, multi-stage cyanidation of concentrate, and countercurrent decantation. Overall gold recovery was 86.8%.
nodes.text: Itogon Gold Plant (Philippines) (фабрика Итогон, Itogon concentrator, Itogon plant (Philippines))

nodes.name: McIntyre Gold Plant (Canada)
nodes.definition: A Canadian gold processing plant (1300 t/d) treating highly pyritized gold ore with fine and coarse gold. It used four-stage crushing, grinding, gravity concentration, flotation, and cyanidation; described as a classic example for pyritic refractory ores.
nodes.text: McIntyre Gold Plant (Canada) (фабрика Мак-Интайр, McIntyre concentrator, McIntyre plant (Canada))

nodes.name: Arthur White Plant (Canada)
nodes.definition: A Canadian gold processing plant (1000 t/d) treating ore from the Dickenson mine with 5-20 g/t Au, containing pyrite, arsenopyrite, sphalerite, and free gold. The flowsheet includes gravity, flotation, and cyanidation, with a fluidized bed roaster for the concentrate.
nodes.text: Arthur White Plant (Canada) (фабрика Артур Вайт (Канада), Arthur White concentrator)

nodes.name: Campbell Red Lake Plant (Canada)
nodes.definition: A gold processing plant in Ontario, Canada, operated by Placer Dome. The mine underwent modernization in 1987 and is known for processing refractory gold ores from the Red Lake district.
nodes.text: Campbell Red Lake Plant (Canada) (Campbell Red Lake gold mine, Campbell mine (Ontario), Campbell Red Lake concentrator)

nodes.name: New Consort Mine
nodes.definition: Золотой рудник компании Eastern Transvaal Consolidated Mines, на котором расположена центральная обжиговая установка. Доля ассоциированного с сульфидами золота в руде Нью-Консорт составляет около 15%.
nodes.text: New Consort Mine (Нью Консорт, New Consort, рудник Нью-Консорт)

nodes.name: Kwekwe Roasting Plant (Zimbabwe)
nodes.definition: A gold processing plant in Kwekwe (Que Que), Zimbabwe, that operated roasting facilities for refractory gold concentrates. The plant provided services to small mines and is referenced in the context of roasting and cyanidation of calcine.
nodes.text: Kwekwe Roasting Plant (Zimbabwe) (Kwekwe gold processing plant, Que Que roasting plant)

nodes.name: Cannon Plant (Washington, USA)
nodes.definition: A modern refractory gold‑silver processing plant with a capacity of 2,200 t/d, treating ore averaging 8 g/t Au and 12 g/t Ag. The flowsheet includes two‑stage grinding, a carbon flotation section after the rod mill producing concentrate with 60–150 g/t Au, followed by sulfide flotation with two cleaner stages. Combined concentrates contain 155 g/t Au and 220 g/t Ag at about 90% recovery.
nodes.text: Cannon Plant (Washington, USA) (Cannon gold plant, Cannon gold plant (Washington), фабрика Кэннои, фабрика Кэннон)

nodes.name: McLaughlin Plant (USA)
nodes.definition: Gold processing plant in California, USA (capacity 3000 t/d) treating highly refractory ores with fine gold (2-5 µm) associated with pyrite, marcasite, arsenopyrite, pyrargyrite and sulfosalts, plus carbonates and active carbonaceous matter. Uses autoclave oxidation at 175°C and 220 kPa, then CIP. Gold recovery 92-93%.
nodes.text: McLaughlin Plant (USA) (McLaughlin gold plant, фабрика Мак-Лафлин)

nodes.name: Mercur Gold Plant
nodes.definition: Gold processing plant in Utah, USA, treating both oxidized and sulfide ores with autoclave oxidation under alkaline conditions, followed by carbon-in-leach cyanidation.
nodes.text: Mercur Gold Plant (Mercur plant, Mercur)

nodes.name: Goldstrike Gold Plant (USA)
nodes.definition: Large gold processing plant in Nevada, USA, owned by American Barrick Corporation, processing refractory sulfide ore with extremely fine gold (50 Å and smaller) locked in pyrite and marcasite.
nodes.text: Goldstrike Gold Plant (USA) (Goldstrike plant, Goldstrike gold processing plant, фабрика Голдстрайк)

nodes.name: Cinola Gold Project
nodes.definition: A gold project referenced in the literature for its radical new processing plans. The source is a brief article in Mining Journal (1994) announcing major changes to the project's development strategy.
nodes.text: Cinola Gold Project (Radical new plans for Cinola project)
aliases: Radical new plans for Cinola project

nodes.name: Austin Gold Plant (USA)
nodes.definition: Золотоизвлекательная фабрика в штате Невада, США, пущенная в 1986 г. Перерабатывает руду сложного состава (сульфиды Fe, As, Sb, углистое вещество) с содержанием Au 6,9 г/т. Производительность 900 т/сут. С 1989 г. применяет бактериальное окисление (фирма «Костич Ресеч») флотационного концентрата с последующим цианированием CIL. Общее извлечение золота 74-78%.
nodes.text: Austin Gold Plant (USA) (фабрика Остин, Austin plant (Nevada))

nodes.name: Tonkin Springs Gold Plant (USA)
nodes.definition: Золотоизвлекательная фабрика в штате Невада, США, введённая в строй в 1989 г. Перерабатывает упорную руду с тонкозернистыми сульфидами, содержанием Au 3,9 г/т, Ag 6,2 г/т, S 1,34%, органического углерода 0,39%. Производительность 1500 т/сут. Применяет бактериальное окисление в 4 реакторах (60 ч) с последующей угольной сорбцией (CIL). Извлечение золота 90%.
nodes.text: Tonkin Springs Gold Plant (USA) (фабрика Тонкин Спрингс, Tonkin Springs plant (Nevada))

nodes.name: Salsigne Gold Mine and Processing Plant
nodes.definition: A gold mine and processing plant in France known for refractory gold-arsenic ores. The plant used oxidative roasting and cyanidation; it was also referenced in the context of technological developments and changes in ownership (sale). The source includes references 759 and 760 in the bibliography.
nodes.text: Salsigne Gold Mine and Processing Plant (Salsigne mine (France), Salsigne gold plant, Salsigne still for sale)

nodes.name: Завод Кова Сейко (Япония)
nodes.definition: Японская компания – основной разработчик и владелец промышленной хлоридовозгоночной технологии извлечения золота, серебра, меди, свинца, цинка и серной кислоты из пиритных концентратов. Реализовала процесс на заводах Тобато (670 т/сут) и Агамасаки (до 28 тыс.т окатышей оксида железа в месяц).
nodes.text: Завод Кова Сейко (Япония) (Kova Seiko Plant, Kova Seiko (Япония), фирма Кова Сейко)

nodes.name: Sigma Gold Plant (Canada)
nodes.definition: A gold processing plant in Quebec, Canada, owned by Placer Dome, with a capacity of 1,300 t/d. Processes quartz-tourmaline ore (4–6 g/t Au) using three-stage grinding in cyanide solution, two-stage cyanidation, and zinc dust precipitation. Gold recovery 95.2%.
nodes.text: Sigma Gold Plant (Canada) (Sigma concentrator (Quebec), Sigma gold concentrator (Quebec), Sigma plant, фабрика Сигма)

nodes.name: Mina Kilduhn Plant
nodes.definition: A gold‑silver processing plant in Mexico that treats manganiferous silver‑gold ores (500 g/t Ag, 2 g/t Au, 4–5 % Mn) by chlorinating roasting with 4 % NaCl at 810 °C in tubular furnaces, followed by cyanidation and Merrill‑Crowe precipitation. The process increased silver recovery from 20 % to 88 % and achieved NaCl regeneration of about 70 % through evaporation of barren solutions.
nodes.text: Mina Kilduhn Plant (Minera Kilduhn, Минера Килдун, Mina Kilduhn factory)

nodes.name: Lupin Gold Mine
nodes.definition: A high‑mechanized gold mine in the Northwest Territories, Canada, operating in permafrost conditions with a 1800 t/d concentrator that treats pyrrhotite‑bearing quartzitic ores by full‑slime cyanidation after intensive aeration to neutralize pyrrhotite.
nodes.text: Lupin Gold Mine (Lupin Mine, Lupin concentrator, Lupin gold plant)

nodes.name: Berengela Segregation-Roasting Pilot Plant (Peru)
nodes.definition: A pilot‑scale facility in Peru that demonstrated the segregation‑roasting‑flotation technology for oxidized copper ores at industrial scale. It is referenced as a key example of successful implementation of the segregation process with gold and silver co‑recovery.
nodes.text: Berengela Segregation-Roasting Pilot Plant (Peru) (опытно-промышленный завод Беренгела, Berengela plant)

nodes.name: Pamour Porcupine Plant
nodes.definition: Canadian gold‑copper processing plant in Ontario, owned by Royal Oak Mines (commissioned 1971, 2700 t/d). Treats cupriferous gold ore by gravity–flotation to produce a copper‑gold concentrate for smelting and a pyrite‑gold concentrate for on‑site cyanidation.
nodes.text: Pamour Porcupine Plant (Pamour Porcupine gold plant, Pamour Porcupine concentrator, фабрика Пэмоур Поркьюпайн, Пэмоур Поркьюпайн)

nodes.name: Kvemont Plant
nodes.definition: Industrial gold‑copper‑zinc processing plant in Canada (capacity ~2250 t/d) treating a complex polymetallic ore containing chalcopyrite, sphalerite, pyrite, pyrrhotite, quartz, and aluminosilicates. The flowsheet includes staged grinding, sequential copper, zinc, and pyrite flotation, and cyanidation of the pyrite concentrate. Detailed reagent regimes and equipment data are documented.
nodes.text: Kvemont Plant (Kvemont concentrator, Kvemont gold‑copper‑zinc plant, Quemont, Квемонт)

nodes.name: Paliden Plant
nodes.definition: Gold processing plant in the Philippines owned by Itogon Suyok Mines, processing copper-gold ore at 430 t/d. The flowsheet includes washing, grinding, gravity concentration, selective flotation, and cyanidation, achieving 90.4% gold recovery and 53.7% copper recovery.
nodes.text: Paliden Plant (Paliden gold processing plant (Philippines), Itogon Paliden plant)

nodes.name: La Luz Plant
nodes.definition: Gold processing plant in Nicaragua treating copper-gold ore (3.3 g/t Au, 0.4% Cu) at 2000 t/d. Uses trommel washing, grinding, flotation with xanthate and aerofloat, cyanidation, and Merrill-Crowe precipitation, achieving 90.3% overall gold recovery.
nodes.text: La Luz Plant (La Luz gold plant (Nicaragua), La Luz Mines plant)

nodes.name: Warrego Plant (Australia)
nodes.definition: Australian concentrator that processes gold‑copper‑bismuth ore. Copper concentrate (24% Cu, 0.7% Bi, 20 g/t Au) is cyanided, and the precipitate is treated with sulfuric acid, roasted, and smelted to produce crude gold. Acid solution is processed in a separate cycle to recover copper.
nodes.text: Warrego Plant (Australia) (Warrego, Warrego concentrator, Warrego gold-copper-bismuth plant (Australia), фабрика Уоррего)

nodes.name: Magma Copper Plant
nodes.definition: Industrial plant in the USA that cyanided a crude molybdenum concentrate (91% MoS2, 1.0% Cu, 13.7 g/t Au) to remove copper and recover gold. The process used conventional cyanidation with two-stage filtration and zinc dust cementation, consuming 25 kg NaCN per ton of concentrate. The resulting precipitate contained 28% Cu, 4850 g/t Au, and 6130 g/t Ag.
nodes.text: Magma Copper Plant (Магма Коппер, Magma Copper)

nodes.name: Damemagami Plant (Canada)
nodes.definition: A Canadian gold processing plant commissioned in 1988, treating sulfide-disseminated ores from the Telbel and Donald La Ronde mines (Felixite host rock). The flowsheet includes gravity, flotation, cyanidation, and carbon-in-pulp recovery, achieving 92% gold and 67% silver recovery at a cost of 11.41 USD/g Au.
nodes.text: Damemagami Plant (Canada) (фабрика Дамэгэми (Канада), Damemagami gold plant, Damemagami concentrator)

nodes.name: Flin Flon Plant (Canada)
nodes.definition: A Canadian base-metal processing plant treating complex copper-zinc-gold-silver ore (2.7% Cu, 4.8% Zn, 2.1 g/t Au, 37.3 g/t Ag). The flowsheet includes selective flotation of copper and zinc concentrates, and cyanidation of zinc flotation tailings with sulfuric acid regeneration of cyanide. Overall gold recovery 89.2%, silver 79.4%.
nodes.text: Flin Flon Plant (Canada) (фабрика Флин-Флон (Канада), Flin Flon concentrator, Hudson Bay Mining and Smelting Flin Flon plant)
aliases: Hudson Bay Mining and Smelting Flin Flon plant

Technico-economic indicators of flotation are directly used to evaluate the economic performance and feasibility of coal flotation processes.
The general flotation method is evaluated using technico-economic indicators that assess its cost efficiency and resource consumption.

Belt Sluice (ленточный шлюз) and Sluice (шлюз, желоб) are both gravity concentration equipment used in placer mining, sharing the same fundamental separation principle but differing in design (conveyor belt vs. stationary trough).

Belt Sluice and Soft-Lined Sluice are both variants of sluice equipment designed to reduce wear and improve recovery of fine particles; the Belt Sluice uses a rubber belt while the Soft-Lined Sluice uses a soft lining material.

Belt Sluice and Vibrational Sluice are both continuous flow concentration devices; the Vibrational Sluice adds vibration to enhance particle stratification, whereas Belt Sluice relies on belt movement.

Belt Sluice and Amalgamation Sluice are both used in gold recovery; Amalgamation Sluice incorporates mercury to capture gold chemically, while Belt Sluice relies on gravity separation, representing alternative technologies for similar applications.

Belt Sluice and Hydraulic Trap both serve as final recovery units for heavy minerals; Hydraulic Trap uses fluid dynamics to trap dense particles, whereas Belt Sluice uses a moving belt and riffles, making them functional analogs with different mechanisms.

Copper hydroxide and copper sulfate are both widely used as fungicides in agriculture; copper hydroxide can replace copper sulfate in formulations to reduce solubility or improve environmental profile, as suggested by later field trials.

In acidic conditions thiosulfate decomposes to elemental sulfur and sulfite ion (S2O3^2- + 2H+ → S + SO3^2- + H2O), establishing a direct causative link from thiosulfate to sulfite.
Thiosulfate can be oxidized to sulfate by strong oxidizing agents (e.g., I2, H2O2) according to S2O3^2- + 4 I2 + 5 H2O → 2 SO4^2- + 8 I- + 10 H+. This reaction is used in iodometric titrations.

Under strongly reducing conditions or via bacterial metabolism, thiosulfate can be reduced to sulfide (e.g., S2O3^2- + 6 e- + 6 H+ → 2 S2- + 3 H2O). This pathway is less common but documented in sulfur‑cycle geochemistry.
Thiosulfate reacts with cyanide to form thiocyanate: S2O3^2- + CN- → SCN- + SO3^2-. This reaction is widely applied in cyanide detoxification and gold ore processing.
